what_happened: Job 20261027-054211-a2n5 added a refusal rule that matched common request words (budget, gate, ci) to governance files. The operator did not review the reading or design before the queue drain ran it. The rule landed and then refused almost any request that used those words. It stopped three drains and also blocked its own fix three times, so the operator had to step in. The verifier passed the job because it judges acceptance criteria, not whether the rule is sound.
cause: Nothing requires a new refusal or classification rule to be measured against real past requests before it lands. Acceptance criteria and the verifier test that the rule exists and fires on its intended cases. Neither measures how often it would wrongly refuse ordinary requests. The rule's own fix is also subject to the rule, so a bad rule can lock itself in. Drain runs jobs without any design review for rules that gate admission.
prevention: Add a check that runs for any change to an admission or refusal rule. It replays the new rule over the recorded past requests (accepted ones included) and reports the share it would newly refuse. The job fails if that share exceeds a set threshold, or if it would refuse any request that was previously accepted and landed, unless a listed exception is declared. The rule's own fix must be exempt from the rule, or there must be a bypass for repairing it. Make this replay a required acceptance criterion for any job that edits refusal logic.
proposed_request: Add a replay check for admission and refusal rules. When a change touches the code or config that decides which requests admission refuses, run the new rules over every past request stored in the records. Report how many were newly refused and list them. Fail the check if more than 2% of previously accepted requests would be refused, or if any previously landed request would be. Tighten the governance-file refusal rule from job 20261027-054211-a2n5 so it no longer refuses on the bare words budget, gate or ci, and only refuses when a request clearly asks to edit a governed file. Show with a test that the replay check flags the current over-broad rule and passes the tightened one, using real past request texts as fixtures. Make sure a job that repairs a refusal rule is not itself refused by that rule.
